structured_output.world_model:
W3 (cost lens), after E002.

What was measured:
- E001: 9 epochs gave 0.7430 accuracy in 9.43 s.
- E002: 10 epochs gave 0.7495 accuracy in 10.55 s.
- So the local slope is about +0.65 pp per epoch for +1.11 s per epoch, about 12% of the run per epoch. That matches my prior (0.5-0.7 pp per epoch, about 11%) and H4.2's 0.3 pp per half epoch.
- Fitting time = fixed + 1.11 × epochs puts fixed cost at about -0.6 s. That can't be right, so per-epoch cost is really about 1.0-1.05 s and timing noise of about 0.1 s is bending the fit. Either way, fixed cost (transfer, eigh whitening, pad) is at most about 0.3 s, under 4% of the run. H3 and H3.2 are small levers, and the ragged batch is already dropped (n//bs).

Accuracy budget:
- From 0.7495, the 3-seed bar (0.753) needs about +0.35 pp, about 0.55 epoch. The 40-seed-safe point (about 0.756) needs about 1 epoch more, so about 11 epochs.
- Eager, that is about 11.6 s. Compiled, with an expected 12-18% cut per epoch, it is about 9.8-10.2 s.
- Every lever is priced in the same currency: 1 pp of accuracy is about 1.5 epochs, about 1.6 s eager or 1.35 s compiled.
- EMA/Lookahead: if it adds 0.2 pp for under 2% time, it saves about 0.3 epoch, a small net win.
- Progressive resizing: saves about 15-20% of time per epoch. If it costs 0.6-1 pp, that has to be repaid with 1-1.5 epochs (about 13-18%), so the net is roughly zero.
- Muon at batch 2000 with CIFAR-10 hyperparameters: likely an accuracy loss on CIFAR-100. Uncertain.

Systems: per-epoch cost is about 1.05 s eager for 48 steps, roughly 22 ms per step. Compile should fuse BN+GELU and the residual add, saving about 12-18%. torch.SGD already uses foreach, so the optimizer change is marginal. The max-autotune risk is autotuning or a recompile leaking into the timed region, or eval exceeding its budget. Warmup in build should prevent both.

Noise: I assume per-seed std of about 0.2-0.35 pp (3-seed SE about 0.15-0.2 pp) and run-to-run time drift of 1-2%. Differences under 0.3 pp in a single run are not resolvable.

Recommended order: compile (pure time) → set epochs to about 10.5-11 to clear 0.756 → EMA → only then resizing/Muon, each judged on net time at equal accuracy.

Unsure about:
- the actual compile speedup under the 4-CPU pin (launch-bound or compute-bound);
- whether the epoch slope flattens above 10 epochs;
- the per-seed std, which sets the margin.

forecasts.reason: Fusing BN+GELU and residual elementwise ops should cut about 12-18% per epoch; the math is unchanged, so accuracy stays within noise.
Expected gain of 0.1-0.3 pp is within 3-seed noise; it is ambiguous whether the run uses 9 or 10 epochs.
Time drift should be under 2%; per-seed std is likely 0.15-0.4 pp.
The tip already drops the ragged batch, so there is nothing near 0.3 s left to save.
Batch 2000 halves the step count, and CIFAR-10 hyperparameters likely lose accuracy on CIFAR-100; Newton-Schulz overhead offsets part of the per-step saving.
Saves about 15% of time but likely costs 0.5-1 pp, beyond the 0.2 pp allowed, and the accuracy repurchase in epochs about cancels the saving.

cruxes: How much of the roughly 1.05 s per epoch is launch- or elementwise-bound rather than conv compute? This sets whether compile saves 8% or 25%, and so the time of the feasible 11-epoch recipe.
Does the epoch-accuracy slope stay at about 0.65 pp per epoch above 10 epochs, or flatten? This sets the cost of the final 0.35-0.65 pp.
What is the per-seed accuracy std? It sets whether the target is 0.753 or 0.756+, a difference of about half an epoch (about 0.5 s).
